Installing toil

Installing toil from npm or from a clone with no npm install, the toil alias for a clone, and installing this skill for Codex, GitHub Copilot or Claude Code

Docs / Installing toil

Check first: if toil version prints an envelope with "ok": true, toil is installed and nothing here is needed. If toil isn’t found but a clone of the toil repository is on the machine, node <clone>/dist/toil.js version is the same thing.

toil needs Node.js 24.14 or later (node --version) and nothing else: no executable, no native module, no install script and no admin rights. On an older Node every command returns UNSUPPORTED_NODE. Windows, macOS and Linux all work the same.

From npm (recommended)

npm install -g @imagile-dev/toil
toil version

With no global install, npx -y @imagile-dev/toil version runs it on demand. Each GitHub release also carries the packed .tgz for offline or mirrored installs: npm install -g ./imagile-dev-toil-<version>.tgz.

toil is not on npm yet. Until its first release, these fail with a 404; install from a clone instead.

From a clone, with no npm install

For a machine that can reach the git host but not the npm registry. Needs Node and git.

git clone https://github.com/imagile-dev/toil.git
node toil/dist/toil.js version

dist/toil.js is committed, and it is the last released toil: each release rebuilds it, and nothing else changes it, so it is the same file that release ships on npm. Newer commits on main are in a clone’s source but not in its bundle until the next release. Until the first release, the committed bundle is the one built when the skill and the clone path were added to main; after that, it is always the last release. It imports only Node’s built-ins, so there is nothing to install.

To type toil instead of node <clone>/dist/toil.js, add an alias to the shell profile, once:

ShellRunEdits
bash, zshnode toil/dist/toil.js setup alias~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc, by SHELL (--shell bash or --shell zsh to choose)
PowerShellnode toil/dist/toil.js setup alias --profile $PROFILEThe profile of the PowerShell you ran it in

Then open a new terminal and run toil version. --profile <file> names any other profile (macOS bash login shells read ~/.bash_profile). The alias is a shell function between two marker lines; nothing else in the file changes, and running it again updates it in place. node toil/dist/toil.js setup remove-alias, with the same flags, takes it out.

  • An agent’s shell may not read the profile. When toil isn’t found there, run node <clone>/dist/toil.js with the same arguments; it’s the same command.
  • Windows PowerShell’s default execution policy runs no profile. If toil isn’t found after opening a new PowerShell, call node <clone>/dist/toil.js directly.
  • Update with git -C toil pull, which brings the newest release. There is nothing to rebuild.

Installing this skill

toil carries this skill inside itself, so the copy it installs always matches the toil that runs it. Install it once, for the agent you use:

toil skill install --allow-write
toil skill install --agent github-copilot --scope project --allow-write
toil skill install --claude --allow-write
--agent--scope user (the default)--scope project
codex (the default; GitHub Copilot reads it too)~/.agents/skills/toil.agents/skills/toil
github-copilot~/.copilot/skills/toil.github/skills/toil
claude-code (--claude)~/.claude/skills/toil.claude/skills/toil

Project scope is the root of the repository you’re in. Installing writes files outside the workspace, so it’s CLI only and needs --allow-write. Every reference file is installed, so an area you set up later is already documented.

There is nothing to update by hand. The description in the installed SKILL.md names the areas and database engines you have connections for (names only, never a host or a credential), so an agent reaches for toil when a task touches one of them. toil rewrites every copy it installed when a connection is added, changed or removed, and when a toil of another version runs, and says so in meta.warnings (SKILL_REWRITTEN); a rewrite that fails is a SKILL_REWRITE_FAILED warning, never a failed command. Connections that only TOIL_* env vars define are named when they’re set in the process that writes the skill, and the output says which. With no connections, the description is the general one.

toil skill show (skill_show over MCP) prints the description toil would write now and every installed copy, with its version and whether it’s current.

toil only ever rewrites a toil folder it installed itself. One copied by hand, or installed by a marketplace, is left exactly as it is, and toil skill install refuses to replace it: move it aside first.

Other ways in, for agents toil doesn’t write to:

  • Claude Code, from the plugin marketplace in the repository: claude plugin marketplace add imagile-dev/toil, then claude plugin install toil@toil (or /plugin marketplace add imagile-dev/toil and /plugin install toil@toil in a session). From a clone, pass its path instead of imagile-dev/toil. This copy carries the general description, and toil doesn’t keep it current.
  • Any installer that reads skills/<name>/SKILL.md from a git repository: point it at https://github.com/imagile-dev/toil.
